## ⚠ THINGS A COLD SEAT SHOULD KNOW BEFORE IT TOUCHES ANYTHING

- ⛔★★ **A SUB-AGENT HAS NO AGENT TOOL.** Only the top-level conductor can launch lanes. Three chain conductors failed on this at #311.
- ⛔★★ **THE SEAT RUNS ONE COMMAND AT A TIME, AND A CALL'S 180 s CLOCK STARTS IN THE QUEUE.** Twelve lanes meant about two minutes of queue before every command. At most two lanes on the seat, one the single committer; text lanes in the cloud, files moved through `device_stage_files` and `device_commit_files`.
- ⛔★★ **THE MOUNT REFUSES UNLINK, SO A NO-OP GIT COMMAND STRANDS A LOCK.** Move it aside (`python3 knowledge/_wrap_commit.py unlock --tag <n>-<seat>`); never `git status`, never `git reset -q` (it strands two).
- ⛔★★ **SURVEY THE COMMITTED TREE WITHOUT `--include-mutating` FIRST.** Step 118 rebuilds the memento index before step 119 checks it, which hid the red CI found on `69848bbe`.
- ⛔★ **START AN OVERNIGHT RUN FROM A FRESH CHAT, AND LAUNCH A WAVE ALL AT ONCE.** His 08:04 words: *"This is my fault we should have started in a fresh lane and stuck to the plan"*.
- ⛔★ **THE BOOT IS THE FIRST USAGE RECORD**, not the fill after the opener reads. The conductor gave him 159,486; the boot was 133,882.
- ✅ **REVIEW PAGES REACH HIM THROUGH THE ARTIFACT "Apollo 304 review"** (v21 to v26 at #311): mirror the published tree under `/home/claude/apollo-review/`, stage the page and its PNGs from the seat, publish with `root` plus a `files` map; pictures inline `<img>` only.
